Use the Context7 MCP tools to fetch up-to-date documentation about **Spring Data JPA projections**.

Steps:
1. Call `resolve-library-id` with "spring data jpa" to find the best matching Context7 library ID. Prefer the official Spring Data JPA library with high trust score and good documentation coverage.
2. Call `query-docs` with the resolved library ID and the query "projections" (interface-based projections, closed/open projections, class-based DTO projections, dynamic projections, native query projections).

Return a clean, well-organized summary of the documentation including:
- The Context7 library ID you used
- Explanation of the different projection types (interface-based closed/open, class-based DTO, dynamic)
- All relevant code examples verbatim (do not paraphrase code)
- Any caveats or notes from the docs

Do not truncate code examples. Return raw documentation content faithfully.

CONSENTE var quando il tipo è ovvio, lambda, Stream API, Optional. Usa quando il progetto è su Java 11 o quando la compatibilità con Java 11 deve essere mantenuta. content.text:
### DTO Projection JPQL Query Rewriting

Source: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-data-jpa/blob/main/src/main/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/repositories/projections.adoc

Demonstrates how Spring Data JPA can rewrite JPQL queries to use constructor expressions for DTO projections. Use this when your JPQL query selects the root entity or multiple columns and you want to map them to a DTO.

```java
interface UserRepository extends Repository<User, Long> {

  @Query("SELECT u FROM User u WHERE u.lastname = :lastname")                       
  List<UserDto> findByLastname(String lastname);

  @Query("SELECT u.firstname, u.lastname FROM User u WHERE u.lastname = :lastname") 
  List<UserDto> findMultipleColumnsByLastname(String lastname);
}

record UserDto(String firstname, String lastname){}
```

### Projections > Using Projections with JPA > String-based queries > Native Queries

Source: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-data-jpa/blob/main/src/main/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/repositories/projections.adoc

When using class-based projections with native queries, if result properties map directly to the DTO's constructor arguments (order and types match), you can declare the DTO type as the query result type. If properties don't match or require transformation, use `@SqlResultSetMapping` to map the result set to the DTO and specify the mapping name in `@NativeQuery`.

--------------------------------

### Projections > Using Projections with JPA > String-based queries > JPQL Queries

Source: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-data-jpa/blob/main/src/main/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/repositories/projections.adoc

For string-based queries (JPQL and native), class-based projections require specific considerations. JPQL uses constructor expressions for class-based projections, requiring a query like `SELECT new com.example.NamesOnly(u.firstname, u.lastname) from User u`. Spring Data JPA can rewrite queries to use constructor expressions if they select the root object, individual properties, or DTO objects. This rewriting is bypassed if the `@Query`-annotated query already uses constructor expressions. Ensure DTO types have an all-args constructor for projection.

--------------------------------

### Projections > Using Projections with JPA > Derived queries

Source: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-data-jpa/blob/main/src/main/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/repositories/projections.adoc

Spring Data JPA uses `Tuple` queries to construct interface proxies for interface-based projections. Query derivation supports both class-based and interface projections by introspecting the returned type. Class-based projections use JPA's instantiation mechanism (constructor expressions) to create the projection instance. Projections limit the selection to top-level properties of the target entity; any nested properties resolving to joins select the entire nested property, causing the full join to materialize.

--------------------------------

### JPA Ahead of Time Repositories

Source: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-data-jpa/blob/main/src/main/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/jpa/aot.adoc

Supported features for JPA AOT repositories include derived query methods, `@Query`/`@NativeQuery` and named query methods, `@Procedure` methods, `@Modifying` methods returning `void` or `int`, `@QueryHints` support, pagination, `Slice`, `Stream`, and `Optional` return types, sort query rewriting, interface and DTO projections, and Value Expressions.
